sources.citation: Idiata-Mayombo, Daniel Franck. 1993. Elements de phonologie diachronique du isangu (B.42). Pholia 8: 67-108. Lyon: CRLS, Universite Lumiere Lyon 2.
sources.note: Nothing. Diachronic phonology of isangu of Mimongo: Proto-Bantu > isangu vowel and consonant reflexes and tonal correspondences for nominals and infinitives (H-HB, H-BB, H-DB, H-MB classes; long vs short radical vowel conditions tone). No mention of accent or stress anywhere in the article (0 hits for 'accent').

sources.citation: Blanchon, Jean A. 1990. The Great *HL Split in Bantu Group B40. Pholia 5: 17-29; and Blanchon, Jean A. 1990. Noms composes en massango et en nzebi de Mbigou (Gabon). Pholia 5: 31-48.
sources.note: Nothing. Tonal reflexes of *HL in i-Sangu/yi-Punu/yi-Lumbu and tonology of compound nouns in massango; no accent/stress statement (0 relevant 'accent'/'stress' hits in either article).

sources.citation: Blanchon, Jean A. 1988. Relevements tonals en eshira et en massango: premiere approche d'une tonologie comparee du groupe bantou B 40. Pholia 3: 71-85.
sources.note: Nothing on word stress. Massango (isangu of Mbigou): progressive and regressive H-tone bridges, downstep, tone-class reflexes; p. 83 characterises the 'rythme' of the massango tonal melody vs punu/lumbu/eshira, a tonal/intonational remark, not a stress rule. (Same volume, Hombert & Mouele 1988 on wanzi B50, p. 193, has a generic aside about 'le role grandissant joue par l'accent sur la premiere syllabe du theme' in the region, naming massango only for a fortis/lenis C1 alternation, not as a stress statement about isangu.)

sources.note: From the title and record only: shows that polysyllabic nouns reflecting the Proto-Bantu *LH (BH) tone type split into two tonal classes in the B.40 and H.12 zones, i.e. a historical-comparative account of noun tone classes; no synchronic tone inventory seen.

sources.citation: Blanchon, Jean Alain. 1999. 'Tone cases' in Bantu group B.40. In Jean A. Blanchon & Denis Creissels (eds.), Issues in Bantu Tonology (Grammatische Analysen afrikanischer Sprachen 10), 37-82. Köln: Rüdiger Köppe. ISBN 978-3-89645-033-3.
sources.tag: likely states tone; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: online with restricted access (login, paywall or limited view)
sources.note: Publisher summary: examines the systems of tonal rules of several B.40 varieties and argues that once language-specific tone rules are discounted all varieties share one and the same set of underlying tonal forms, corresponding to the proto-language ('tone cases' = tonal shapes nominals take by syntactic context); results linked to the author's earlier zone H study. Tone inventory of isangu not stated in what was seen.
sources.venue: Issues in Bantu Tonology (Grammatische Analysen afrikanischer Sprachen 10)
